title: Quantifying the detection likelihood of faint peaks in interferometric data through jackknifing: Test application on finding z > 10 galaxy candidates
question: How to quantify the detection likelihood of faint line peaks in interferometric data by jackknifing visibilities, tested on tentative [O III] 88 um detections toward three z>10 galaxy candidates

recipe.method: Average calibrated visibilities in time and frequency, subtract a first-order continuum with uvcontsub, then image with tclean
key_parameters: time averaging 30 s; spectral averaging ~30 MHz bins without interpolation on the frequency axis

recipe.method: Randomly flip the sign of half of the visibilities in the visibility plane with different random seeds, then re-image each realization with the same imaging as the real data
key_parameters: 50 jackknife realizations per observation, ~9 min per iteration on a 2019 MacBook Pro
assumptions: Visibility noise is additive, Gaussian, uncorrelated and zero-mean for well-calibrated data

recipe.goal: Find peaks in real and jackknifed cubes
recipe.method: Run FindClump (interferopy, SExtractor-based) on the real cube and each jackknifed cube, keep positive peaks within 0.6 arcsec of the optical centre, to build P_D and P_FD
key_parameters: peaks above S/N of 0 retained; duplicates merged within 0.2 arcsec and 0.2 GHz
SExtractor analysis and detection thresholds both set to 2

recipe.goal: Likelihood ratio test for blind line detection
recipe.method: Compute false-detection likelihood L_FD(gamma) from jackknifed peak PDF, multiply by number of real peaks for expected noise count, and form Lambda = L_D/L_FD; significant if Lambda >= k = 3
key_parameters: detection threshold gamma = 4 sigma, critical value k = 3
assumptions: Jackknifed peaks sample the false-detection distribution; peak distribution is a subset of the pixel-value distribution of a smoothed random Gaussian field

recipe.goal: Apply JWST redshift prior to GLASS-z12
recipe.method: Multiply the PDFs by Gaussian prior on redshift, uniform prior on radial distance and uniform prior on peak S/N in post-processing with Bayes theorem, then renormalise
key_parameters: Gaussian redshift prior mu = 12.33, sigma = 0.02 (+/-0.4 GHz at 254.54 GHz); uniform radial prior 0 to 0.6 arcsec; uniform S/N prior from 2.5; only peaks with S/N > 2.5 counted
assumptions: No correlation between peak S/N and its RA, Dec or frequency position for non-primary-beam-corrected maps
